title: Kubernetes security flashcards: for the KCSA exam
description: Cloud native and Kubernetes security for the KCSA exam, from the Kubernetes documentation and NIST: every security idea explained before it is tested. Builds on the Kubernetes (KCNA) deck.

glossary.AES: Advanced Encryption Standard, a widely used symmetric cipher
glossary.ALL: in a capabilities list, every Linux capability at once
glossary.CHOWN: a Linux capability: change the owner of a file
glossary.CN: Common Name, the name field in a certificate's subject
glossary.CSV: comma-separated values, a plain-text table format
glossary.DELETE: the HTTP method for removing a resource
glossary.FOWNER: a Linux capability: bypass permission checks that normally require owning the file
glossary.FSETID: a Linux capability: keep a file's set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits when it is changed
glossary.GCM: Galois/Counter Mode, a way of running a block cipher such as AES that also checks integrity
glossary.HEAD: the HTTP method that fetches only a resource's headers
glossary.HOME: the environment variable that holds a user's home directory
glossary.HTTPS: HTTP sent over an encrypted TLS connection
glossary.ICMP: Internet Control Message Protocol, used by tools such as ping
glossary.LDAP: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol, used to look up users and groups in a directory
glossary.MKNOD: a Linux capability: create special files such as device files
glossary.MTU: maximum transmission unit, the largest packet a network link carries
glossary.NAT: network address translation, rewriting packet addresses as they pass a router
glossary.OSI: the Open Systems Interconnection model, which describes networking in seven layers
glossary.PATCH: the HTTP method for changing part of a resource
glossary.PEM: a text encoding for certificates and keys, the files that begin "-----BEGIN"
glossary.PKCS: Public-Key Cryptography Standards, a family of formats for keys and certificates
glossary.POST: the HTTP method for creating a resource
glossary.PUT: the HTTP method for replacing a resource
glossary.SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language, an older single sign-on standard
glossary.SCTP: Stream Control Transmission Protocol, a transport protocol like TCP
glossary.SETGID: a Linux capability: change the group ID of a process
glossary.SSH: Secure Shell, an encrypted remote login protocol
glossary.SSL: Secure Sockets Layer, the predecessor of TLS
glossary.TCP: Transmission Control Protocol, the reliable transport most traffic uses
glossary.UDP: User Datagram Protocol, a connectionless transport
glossary.USB: Universal Serial Bus, as in a USB stick

checks.what: Two independent audits read all 1096 cards against the Kubernetes v1.37 documentation, the CNCF security whitepapers, NIST publications and the other cited sources, for accuracy, currency and plain language
checks.result: 32 wrong answers, 76 unsupported claims, 15 ambiguous cards, 20 unclear ones and 121 minor issues were fixed. Version-dependent facts are marked volatile against v1.37. Cards built on sources that are not openly licensed (Sigstore, SLSA, MITRE ATT&CK, SPIFFE) state facts in our own words and say so.
